Need to generate tests that exercise builder, getInstance, checkVersion, normalizeMetaSchemaUri, isYaml, idMatchesSourceUri, getSchema overloads, etc. Since many dependencies (URIFactory, URIFetcher, JsonMetaSchema, JsonSchema, ValidationContext) are complex; we can use mocking (e.g., Mockito) to isolate behavior. However requirement only says generate JUnit 4 test cases; we can assume we have access to necessary classes. For simplicity, we can test static methods (checkVersion, normalizeMetaSchemaUri, isYaml) and builder validation errors.

We can also test that constructor throws IllegalArgumentException when parameters invalid by calling builder().objectMapper(null) etc. But builder's build uses internal validation: need to supply defaultMetaSchemaURI and meta schemas.

We can create a dummy JsonMetaSchema implementation that returns a fixed URI and readId returns null. Or we can use existing meta schemas from library; but not given. For test isolation, we can create a minimal stub subclass of JsonMetaSchema (abstract?). Let's inspect JsonMetaSchema class? Not provided. Might be abstract with many methods. Hard.

Alternative: focus on static utility methods that don't need heavy dependencies: checkVersion, normalizeMetaSchemaUri, isYaml, and builder's defaultMetaSchemaURI handling via getInstance which uses known version classes. Those classes (Version4 etc.) likely exist in library. Could rely on them.

Simplify: write tests for checkVersion returns correct type, throws for unknown, and for null returns null.

Test normalizeMetaSchemaUri transforms http to https, preserves other components, throws for invalid URI.

Test isYaml returns true for .yaml/.yml and false otherwise.

Test idMatchesSourceUri: need JsonMetaSchema with readId method; we can create a mock using Mockito.

Similarly test getSchema with invalid JSON string causes JsonSchemaException.

We can also test that getUriTranslator returns a translator that maps based on uriMap.

But we can limit to covering most branches.

Write test class JsonSchemaFactoryTest with @RunWith(MockitoJUnitRunner.class) to use mocks.

Will need imports for org.junit, static org.junit.Assert.* , org.mockito.*.

Write test methods:

- testCheckVersionValidFlags

- testCheckVersionInvalidFlag (pass null? Actually null returns null; unknown enum not possible). Use a fake enum? Not needed.

- testNormalizeMetaSchemaUriValidHttp -> expects https.

- testNormalizeMetaSchemaUriInvalid -> expects JsonSchemaException.

- testIsYamlTrueYml, testIsYamlTrueYaml, testIsYamlFalse.

- testIdMatchesSourceUriMatches and not matches using mock JsonMetaSchema.

- testGetSchemaInvalidJsonStringThrowsException.

- testBuilderNullObjectMapperThrowsInBuild: create builder, set objectMapper(null), set yamlMapper(new YAMLMapper()), defaultMetaSchemaURI="http://example.com/schema", add dummy meta schema, then build expecting IllegalArgumentException.

Need dummy JsonMetaSchema: we can mock JsonMetaSchema with getUri() returning "http://example.com/schema". Also readId may be needed for findMetaSchemaForSchema. But for builder validation we only need jsonMetaSchemas map not empty and containing defaultMetaSchemaURI normalized. So create mock JsonMetaSchema with getUri() returning "http://example.com/schema". Also need any other methods? Not used.

When builder.build called, it constructs JsonSchemaFactory passing jsonMetaSchemas map, etc. It will call normalizeMetaSchemaUri on defaultMetaSchemaURI inside builder? Actually in build it passes defaultMetaSchemaURI (as set) unchanged; then JsonSchemaFactory constructor validates jsonMetaSchemas.get(normalizeMetaSchemaUri(defaultMetaSchemaURI)) != null. So we need to ensure map contains key normalized. The builder's addMetaSchema will normalize the meta schema's uri. So we need to addMetaSchema(mockMetaSchema) before build.

Thus builder = JsonSchemaFactory.builder().objectMapper(new ObjectMapper()).yamlMapper(new YAMLMapper()).defaultMetaSchemaURI("http://example.com/schema").addMetaSchema(mockMetaSchema).build();

But we also need to test null objectMapper case: set objectMapper(null). That will cause IllegalArgumentException in constructor.

Ok.

Also test getInstance returns non-null and default meta schema matches version.

But that's more integration.

We'll provide tests.
